name: Genitive Subject in a Gerund-Participial

1.definition: Expresses an overt subject in the genitive inside a gerund-participial.

relatedConstructions.notes: Compare We objected to their blocking the exit and We objected to them blocking the exit. The case varies in this frame. Availability depends on the higher construction and variety.
Their carefully sorting the files has a verbal predicate with an adverb and direct object. Their careful sorting of the files has adjective and of-complement in a nominal.

projection.target: The verb can retain adverbial modification and take a direct object. The genitive marks its subject rather than turning the following verb into a noun.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Their arriving so late
curious.summary: A word like their can sit in front of a verb ending in -ing to say who is doing the action.
curious.body:
In I disliked their arriving so late, the word their says who arrived. What follows is still verb-like: arriving keeps its own add-on, so late. The word their marks the one who does the action, rather than turning arriving into an ordinary noun.

The same job can be done by a different form. We objected to their blocking the exit and We objected to them blocking the exit both fit. This dictionary notes that which form is available depends on the larger pattern and on the variety of English.

examples.text: We objected to [their blocking the exit].
We objected to [them blocking the exit].

curious.try: Say We objected to their blocking the exit, then We objected to them blocking the exit. Which one would you say, and does the other sound natural to you?

teacher.summary: Useful when students ask why a genitive appears before a verb in -ing, or how it differs from a noun with of.
teacher.explain: This is a gerund-participial clause whose subject is an overt genitive NP: their arriving so late, with their as subject and arriving so late as the verb phrase. This dictionary’s key point is that the verb stays verbal. It can keep adverbial modification and take a direct object, so the genitive marks the subject and does not turn the -ing word into a noun. An oblique subject is an alternative in some frames (them blocking the exit); this dictionary says the case varies and that availability depends on the higher construction and variety. This analysis is marked provisional in this dictionary.
teacher.terms: Gerund-participial is the CGEL-style label for the clause. Traditional grammars may call the -ing word a gerund.

examples.text: We objected to [their blocking the exit].
We objected to [them blocking the exit].

contrasts.text: Their careful sorting of the files

watch_for: A learner might treat their arriving as a noun phrase with an ordinary noun, when the -ing word keeps verb features such as adverbs and a direct object.
A learner might treat their blocking the exit and their blocking of the exit as the same structure.
teacher.activity: Give pairs a short list of -ing phrases with a genitive in front. Students add an adverb or a direct object to each (their arriving ...), then try a version with careful and of, and say which one keeps the verb's own add-ons.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Genitive Subject in a Gerund-Participial." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/genitive-ing-subject-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
